site.title: Echelon | Interschool tech fest at Bangalore International School
site.description: Echelon is an interschool tech fest for students in Grades 8–12, run by Bangalore International School in collaboration with Vidyashilp University. Eight events to code, build, pitch and race.

event.name: Echelon
event.tagline: Like migrating birds, we rise in formation.
event.summary: The interschool tech fest for Grades 8–12. Eight events to code, build, pitch and race, run in collaboration with Vidyashilp University.
event._dateHelp: Set date to an ISO date with the India offset, for example 2027-01-16T08:30:00+05:30. Leave it empty to show 'Date to be announced'.

about.statement: Code it. Build it. Pitch it. Race it.
about.heading: Built for students who like making things work
paragraphs: Echelon is an interschool tech fest run by Bangalore International School in collaboration with Vidyashilp University.

Students in Grades 8–12 form teams, represent their school and compete in hands-on events, from tracing code to break out of an escape room to building an expert system in Prolog and racing a drone through a course.

name.heading: Every letter stands for something
name._help: From the official Echelon logo. Keep one word per letter of ECHELON, in order; the build checks this. The same words are drawn around the logo in src/logo.js (WORDS).

cards.title: Eight ways to compete
cards.text: Code breaking, logic puzzles, web and game design, building with e-waste, drone racing, app pitches and AI with Prolog.

cards.title: Teams from your school
cards.text: Team up with classmates and go up against students from other schools.

cards.title: One day on campus
cards.text: Everything happens at Bangalore International School, from 8:15 am to 2:30 pm. Breakfast and lunch are provided.

steps.title: Pick your events
steps.text: Eight events, from breaking code in an escape room to racing a drone. Each card lists its time, its room and what you need to know.

steps.title: Form a team
steps.text: Teams of three. Each school can enter up to two teams in every event.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Sign your team up on the official registration form.

steps.title: Compete
steps.text: Report at Bangalore International School by 8:15 am and compete against other schools.

events.heading: Eight events. Pick yours.
events.intro: Every event has its own time and room. Open the details for the rules and what to bring.

items.name: Escape Room – Code Breakers
items.summary: Trace the code, work out its output and break your way through the challenge.
items.priorKnowledge: Trace tables, and pseudocode, Python or Java (your choice)
about: Solve programming challenges using trace tables.
Questions may use pseudocode, Python or Java, in the language your team chooses.
Analyse the code, trace its execution and arrive at the correct output to progress through the challenge.

items.name: Treasure Hunt – Logic & Discovery
items.summary: Crack codes, puzzles and graphs to uncover the clues and reach the final destination.
items.venue: Starts in the First Floor Computer Lab
about: Put your logical thinking and problem-solving skills to the test.
Solve a series of challenges that may include decryption, logic puzzles, mathematical reasoning and graphing tasks.
Each one uncovers a clue that leads you on to the final destination.

items.name: Web Designing
items.summary: Design and build a website from scratch with HTML and a scripting language of your choice.
items.priorKnowledge: HTML and a scripting language of your choice
items.resources: Bring all your images, audio and video files saved on your device
about: Design and develop a website using HTML and any scripting language you like.
rules: Pre-designed templates and AI tools aren’t allowed.
Internet access is turned off during the competition.
Bring every resource you need, including images, audio and video, saved locally on your devices.

items.name: Game Designing
items.summary: Create an original game on the platform of your choice, then show the judges how it works.
items.priorKnowledge: A game-making platform of your choice
items.resources: Bring your own device, or use the Windows PCs in the lab
about: Create an original game using any gaming platform you like.
Demonstrate your game, and explain its code, logic and how it works, to the assessment panel.
rules: AI tools aren’t allowed, and this is monitored.

items.name: E-Waste to Innovation – Product Design
items.summary: Turn electronic waste into a useful, innovative or sustainable product.
items.resources: Bring your own materials, mainly e-waste
about: Transform electronic waste into a useful, innovative or sustainable product.
Build a working product or prototype during the competition.
rules: Products are judged on creativity, usefulness, sustainability and how well you use your materials.

items.name: Drone Racing – Precision Challenge
items.summary: Fly your drone through the course with precision, stability and control.
items.resources: Your own drone and fully charged batteries; spares strongly advised
about: Navigate your drone through the designated course, showing precision, stability and control.
You’re assessed on navigation accuracy, steadiness and control, following the competition rules.
rules: Drones can be at most 30 cm × 30 cm.
One drone can be shared by more than one team.
Bring fully charged batteries. Spare drones and batteries are strongly advised.
The school doesn’t provide drones or batteries.

items.name: Shark Tank – The App Innovation Pitch
items.summary: Pitch an app that solves a real-world problem to the jury.
items.resources: Your own device, a pen drive, or Google Slides shared in advance
about: Have an app idea that solves a real-world problem? Identify an unmet need, propose your solution and pitch it to the jury.
Present your app concept, the problem it addresses, its target users and how your solution adds value.
rules: You get 3 to 5 minutes to present.
Bring your presentation on your own device or a pen drive, or share your Google Slides, with your team name and school name, with mahenthren@bischool.in before 19 November 2026.

items.name: Artificial Intelligence – Prolog Expert System Challenge
items.summary: Build a knowledge-based expert system in SWI-Prolog that reasons its way to answers.
about: Design and develop a knowledge-based expert system using SWI-Prolog.
Create a knowledge base of facts and logical rules for a domain of your choice.
Demonstrate how your system answers a set of queries by reasoning over the knowledge base.
rules: Systems are assessed on the accuracy and relevance of their facts, the correctness of their rules, how well they infer conclusions from queries, and how well your team understands the logic.
Be ready to demonstrate your program and explain how your expert system works to the assessment panel.

schedule.heading: One day on campus
schedule.intro: The clock runs from reporting time to prize distribution as you scroll.

before.title: Register your teams
before.text: Sign up on the official registration form.

before.title: Shark Tank slides
before.text: Pitching from Google Slides? Share them, with your team name and school name, with mahenthren@bischool.in before 19 November 2026.

day.title: Reporting, registration and breakfast
day.text: Teams arrive, check in and have breakfast, until 9:00 am.

day.title: Competitions begin
day.text: Seven events start at 9:30 and finish between 10:00 am and 12:30 pm. Treasure Hunt runs from 10:15 to 10:45 am.

schedule._dayNote: From the Echelon 4.0 programme document. Each event's own time and room are on its card.

items.a: Through the official registration form linked on this page. It opens in a new tab. This website doesn't collect any details itself.

items.q: How big is a team, and how many can a school send?
items.a: Every team has three students, and each school can enter up to two teams in each event.
Not in Web Designing or Game Designing, where it's monitored. Web Designing also bans pre-designed templates and turns the internet off.
On Saturday, 21 November 2026, at Bangalore International School. Report by 8:15 am. The day ends with prize distribution, from 1:30 to 2:30 pm.
Yes. Breakfast (8:15 to 9:00 am) and lunch (12:45 to 1:20 pm) are provided.

Web Designing: all your images, audio and video saved on your device, as there's no internet. Game Designing: your own device, or use the lab's Windows PCs. E-Waste to Innovation: your own materials, mainly e-waste. Drone Racing: your drone (at most 30 × 30 cm) with fully charged batteries, plus spares; the school doesn't provide any. Shark Tank: your slides on a device or pen drive, or shared in advance.

items.q: Who do we contact with questions?
items.a: Email the organising team at malarvizhi@bischool.in.
